title: What is known about 1RB1RD_0RC0RD_0LD1LE_1LC0RB_1LF---_1LA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_0RC0RD_0LD1LE_1LC0RB_1LF---_1LA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, decoded. The tape is (10)x 0y; each pass a front halves the blocks of pairs, with a binary cascade of resets (README, "The pass map"). Rarely the pass ends in a restart: the machine replays its own run from blank inside a buffer of 0s, and the buffer mod 3 decides: 0 merges, 2 halts, 1 is not decoded yet. By the model the first restart (event 975,986, about 7·1018 steps) merges, and there is no other in 4.29·1010 passes (around 1032 steps).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 2,604 cells have been visited and 1,710 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.16·10<sup>16</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 2)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/py/bbtools/rleaccel_rec.py (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed in one step, cycle jumps used only after a symbolic proof of the one-cycle rule, and proofs that may themselves apply earlier rules to symbolic lengths, with exact polynomial step counts; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 67,260,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 300 seconds. That is more than 7.16·1016 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.314). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.367).

claims.title: The front's cycle, and k cycles at once
claims.text: L 1 0 (00)m D> (10)b+2 R reaches L 1 0 1 0 (00)m+1 D> (10)b R in 28m + 30 steps; by induction, k cycles take a block of 2k pairs to k pairs and 2k zeros in 28mk + 14k2 + 16k steps. Also the fill rule (the word 0 1 1 1 0 walking left through 0s, 13 steps a cell) and the sweep from the right end to the left end.

claims.title: The pass map agrees with the machine
claims.text: The pass map of the README (left resets while b is odd, a crossing, right resets while b is even) gives the next event exactly for all 1,396 events from blank tape up to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps and for 300 random starts; the restart formula holds on all 542 restarting starts with x < 1,100, y < 16; the merge (buffer 0 mod 3) and the halt (buffer 2 mod 3) on 40 random restarts.

claims.title: Halting tapes of the run's own shape
claims.text: (10)<sup>2<sup>m</sup>+4</sup> 0<sup>2m−6</sup> halts for m = 3 to 9 (the exact simulator); each of them is a restart with buffer 5, 2 mod 3.

claims.title: The run from blank by the model
claims.text: Iterating the pass map with the restart rules: the first restart is at event 975,986 (x = 2,497,092, y = 6, about 7·10<sup>18</sup> steps), buffer 156,069 = 0 mod 3, so it merges after 52,023 replayed passes; then no restart through pass 4.29·10<sup>10</sup> (width 2.2·10<sup>11</sup>, 10<sup>32</sup> to 10<sup>33</sup> steps). Not a proof: the rules are checked on many cases, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if and only if (by the decoded rules) the run reaches a restart whose buffer is 2 mod 3; the nested case (buffer 1 mod 3) is not decoded yet.

check: g++ -O2 -o rleaccel tools/c/rleaccel.cpp && timeout 1800 ./rleaccel 1RB1RD_0RC0RD_0LD1LE_1LC0RB_1LF---_1LA0LE 2 1000000000000000 run.ck 300    # 30 minutes

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but the run is now decoded: a front halves blocks of 10 pairs, a binary cascade of resets makes the jumps, and rare restarts replay the whole run from blank inside a buffer. A restart whose buffer is 2 mod 3 halts the machine.

facts.text: No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 2).
No halt in the C simulator; 2,604 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
One cycle of the front, and k cycles by induction (front_cycles), proved in Lean.
The pass map gives every event from blank tape to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps exactly.
By the model: one restart (merges, buffer 0 mod 3) in the first 4.29·10<sup>10</sup> passes.

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: At the moments the head steps onto a new cell at the right end in state C, the tape is almost always (10)x 0y, and the width 2x + y grows by 4 per event. Between events x jumps by an amount that depends on the binary digits of x − 5 and y/2 + 1: the next two sections give the exact rule.

sections.heading: The pass map: a front that halves blocks
sections.html:
Between two visits of the right end the head makes one pass. Going left it turns the 0 block into pairs, (10)x 0y → (10)x−2 11 (10)y/2+1 (Lean: sweep_left). Going right, a front (10)a 0z ▷ (10)b halves each block of pairs: one cycle eats two pairs ahead and leaves one pair and two 0s behind, (a, z, b) → (a+1, z+2, b−2) (Lean: cycle, and front_cycles for k cycles at once).

At the end of a block only the parity of b matters. Odd at the separator 11: a reset, the 0s behind the front are turned back into pairs and become the block ahead, b = (z+3)/2. Even at the separator: the front crosses into the right block. At the right end, odd b ends the pass and even b resets again. Repeated resets halve b − 1 (left block) or b − 2 (right block) until it is odd, so the number of resets is a 2-adic valuation: that is the irregular jump of x.





The panel applies the pass map (py/passmap.py, checked against the machine on all 1,396 events from
blank tape to 2·1010 steps and on 300 random starts). It is arithmetic on the rules, not the machine.

sections.heading: Restarts: the run replays itself
sections.html:
When the left block resets more times than the right block has pairs, the pass ends differently: the next event is (10)X 0Y 10 0000 with Y = 2j(z−4)+1 (j the shortfall). The 10 0000 on the right is the tape of the run from blank after 13 steps, and from there the machine replays its own run from blank tape, event for event, to the right of a wall of X pairs, while the buffer of Y zeros between them shrinks by 3 a pass. When the buffer runs out, Y mod 3 decides:

  • 0 mod 3: the copy merges into the wall; the next event is (X + x, y), with (x, y) the blank run's event number Y/3 + 1.
  • 2 mod 3: the machine halts. For example (10)2m+4 02m−6 halts for m = 3 to 9 (its restart has buffer 5).
  • 1 mod 3: the wall itself is cut down and a new buffer appears (not decoded yet).

So the machine halts exactly when (as far as the rules go) its run reaches a restart whose buffer is 2 mod 3. By the model, the run from blank has its first restart at the 975,986th event (x = 2,497,092, y = 6, about 7·1018 steps): buffer 156,069 = 0 mod 3, a merge after 52,023 replayed passes. After that the model finds no restart up to pass 4.29·1010 (width 2.2·1011, roughly 1032–1033 steps).

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is E reading 1. A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (bbtools.ctl) covers the run but still allows halts, with only a local constraint near the head: the head cell and the cells to its right read one of 101010, 101011, 101110, 111010, 111011. Nothing confines a halt to an edge.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.314). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.367).
After 109 steps the tape spans 2,604 cells (1,230 left of the start, 927 right), with a density of 1s of 0.657.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Decoded: a front halves blocks of 10 pairs with a binary cascade of resets (exact pass map, matches all simulated passes). Rare restarts replay the run from blank inside a buffer; a buffer 2 mod 3 halts. Model: one restart (merges) in 4.29e10 passes, ~1e32 steps.
family: two-block bouncer with a binary halving cascade and self-similar restarts
